sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A Cover Art Archive outage was recorded as "this release has no artwork" and kept on disk for a week. Any non-OK answer from the archive's metadata API — a 503, a 429, a gateway error — was written to the IndexedDB cache exactly like a genuine "no such release" 404. Every later visit to any page listing that release then read the stored zero, showed no artwork, and made no request and no warning at all. Only a definitive 404/410 is persisted now; a transport failure is remembered for the current session alone, so a reload or the ⟳ retry button asks again. This is the same distinction the image-byte path, the ⏱ millisecond Length feature and the Relationships column already made — the oldest network path was the one that never got it.

The ⟳ artwork retry button could not recover such a release. It cleared the in-memory caches but never the IndexedDB record, so the re-fetch it triggered read that record straight back and issued no request — the button did nothing at all for every entity that had a stored result. It now evicts the table's cached archive metadata first, which is what the help text already promised it did.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The archive metadata cache now keeps entries for 30 days instead of 7 (⚙️ Settings → 🗄️ ART ARCHIVE INDEXEDDB CACHE → "Metadata (JSON) cache TTL (days)"), matching the image, Relationships and millisecond-length caches, which were all already 30. Fewer repeat requests to coverartarchive.org on pages you revisit. This was only safe to raise once the fix above landed — otherwise one bad minute at the archive would have hidden real artwork for a month rather than a week. If you have ever pressed Save in the settings dialog your stored value is still 7; reset that one field to pick up the new default.
